messages.content: 計算在投擲100次硬幣，每次獲得正面的機率為0.5的情況下，觀察到60次正面的機率。

function.name: calc_binomial_prob
function.description: Calculates the probability of an outcome based on the binomial distribution Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

num_success.description: Number of times the event of interest has occurred.

prob_success.description: Probability of the event of interest on any single experiment. This is a float type value.

message.reasoning: The user asks: "計算在投擲100次硬幣，每次獲得正面的機率為0.5的情況下，觀察到60次正面的機率。" That is: compute probability of observing 60 heads out of 100 flips with p=0.5. So it's binomial probability: C(100,60)*(0.5)^60*(0.5)^40 = C(100,60)*(0.5)^100. We can compute numeric value. Use function calc_binomial_prob. Provide arguments: num_trials=100, num_success=60, prob_success=0.5. Then output result. Probably also mention approximate value. Let's compute approximate: C(100,60) = 100 choose 60 = 100 choose 40. 100 choose 40 is huge. But we can compute approximate probability. Let's approximate using normal approximation: mean=50, variance=25, sd=5. z = (60-50)/5 = 2. So probability of exactly 60? Actually binomial probability at k=60. Use normal approximation with continuity correction: P(59.5< X < 60.5). z1=(59.5-50)/5=1.9, z2=(60.5-50)/5=2.1. Probability ~ phi(2.1)-phi(1.9). phi(2.1)=0.98214, phi(1.9)=0.9713. Difference ~0.01084. So about 0.0108. But exact probability maybe around 0.0108. Let's compute exact: C(100,60) = 100!/(60!40!). We can approximate using log. But we can use function. We'll call function.
